appraisal_events.evidence: on lui avait donné, dans un autre milieu, le surnom, que nous ignorions, de « ni fleurs ni couronnes »... ce qui lui valait ces mots: « Vous, on ne vous dit pas merci. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The cousin's tireless, unstoppable eagerness to attend the dying and funerals earns him a mocking funeral-themed nickname behind his back and a pointedly backhanded lack of thanks, so his conscientiousness is deflated by irony even as it is acknowledged.

appraisal_events.evidence: maman, qui pensait aux autres au milieu de la plus immense douleur, lui dirait... : « Promettez-moi que vous ne viendrez pas... Faites-le pour elle. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator directly credits his mother with thinking of others even amid overwhelming grief, elevating her through this endorsed characterization, in implicit contrast to the cousin's obliviousness.

status_effects.explanation: The cousin comes off worse locally: his relentless presence at the dying and at funerals is rewarded elsewhere with a mocking nickname and, within the family, with pointed non-gratitude, despite his genuine diligence.
Maman is locally elevated by the narrator's admiring note that she thinks of others even in the depths of her own grief.

ambiguities: The passage refers to the diminished figure only as 'il' before he is identified within the same passage as 'mon cousin'/'le cousin'; this identification is inferred from narrative continuity rather than an explicit named antecedent in the supplied text, and the cousin does not appear on the reference sheet.

The line « Vous, on ne vous dit pas merci » could be read either as pure backhanded mockery or as affectionate, teasing acknowledgment of his reliability; the narrative stance toward the cousin is deliberately layered and not fully resolved.
